_comment: Prediction gate policy. These are POLICY thresholds, not fitted parameters: the gate decides whether a probability may be published, it never changes one. Nothing here was selected by scoring the test segment.
_minPriorMatchesPerTeam: A side with ZERO prior matches is refused: its snapshot IS the prior, so the published number would describe the opponent and the competition rather than this team. 1 is the declared default - only the zero case is refused. Raising it to 2 or 5 is a legitimate product choice and the README reports what each setting costs in coverage.
_minEffectiveMatchesPerTeam: Staleness net: evidence so old that its decayed weight has almost vanished. With the validated halfLifeDays=100000 there is effectively no decay, so this check is dormant by design and exists for configurations that do decay. It is deliberately BELOW minPriorMatchesPerTeam: at 1.0 it fired on 533 matches whose weaker side had exactly one prior match, purely because a 2% decay shaved the effective count below the integer bound. Refusing those matches may be reasonable, but it must be stated as policy through minPriorMatchesPerTeam, not arrive as a rounding artefact.
_minCompetitionMatchesObserved: Matches the frozen context's own MinBaselineSamples: below it the goal baseline is a config seed rather than learned data, so the lambda scale is not measured.
_lambdaClamp: The frozen model's own clamp. The gate does not apply it - it only refuses a prediction whose lambda is SITTING on it, because such a value is saturated rather than measured.
_confidence: Prior-match thresholds, set by the WEAKER side. Confidence describes the evidence and never the probability - the classifier's input type carries no probability field at all.
